chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you arrive at Mina, say: O Allah, this is Mina, and it is from what You have favored upon us among the rituals. So I ask You to favor upon us with what You have favored upon Your prophets. Indeed, I am Your servant and in Your hold.'

Then you should pray Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, the last Isha, and Fajr there; and the Imam prays Dhuhr there, and nothing else is permissible for him. It is permissible for you to pray elsewhere if you are unable. Then you join them at Arafat.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'And the boundary of Mina is from Al-Aqaba to the valley of Muhassar.'

key_terms.الْعَقَبَة: Al-Aqaba, a landmark defining the boundary of Mina
key_terms.عَرَفَات: Arafat, the main station of Hajj
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a sacred site near Mecca used for Hajj rituals
key_terms.وَادِي مُحَسِّر: Valley of Muhassar, another landmark defining the boundary of Mina

ai.seo_question: What are the specific prayers and supplications required when arriving at Mina during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the ritual etiquette for arriving at Mina, emphasizing a supplication that links the pilgrim's status to the blessings granted to the Prophets, thereby reinforcing the Shia emphasis on imitative devotion. It clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between the Imam's obligatory single prayer (Dhuhr) and the pilgrim's flexibility, while precisely defining Mina's boundaries from the Aqaba to Wadi Muhassir, a key reference for Shia fiqh of Hajj.
